title: Implement longest increasing subsequence in Rust
description: Implement lis_length(nums: &[i32]) -> usize using O(n log n) patience sorting: maintain a tails array and binary search for each element.

task_spec.prompt:
Implement lis_length in src/lib.rs using patience sorting:
- Maintain a `tails: Vec<i32>` (tails[i] = smallest tail of IS of length i+1)
- For each num: use binary_search to find position
  - If Ok(_) (exact match): skip (strictly increasing, no duplicates extend)
  - If Err(pos): if pos==tails.len() push num, else replace tails[pos]=num
- Return tails.len()
All 5 cargo test cases must pass.
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test --quiet` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `cargo test --quiet` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
